F1: When there is no destination calendar, `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` gives `undefined`, and line 119 then reads `.integration` on it, so a Google Meet booking crashes with a TypeError.
F2: The fallback only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but it then compares `cal.externalId` to that falsy value, so it never matches; update gets `calendarId: undefined` and delete falls back to "primary".
F3: selectedCalendar` only matches a destination with the same `credentialId`, so credential-less destinations (which EventManager still handles at 375-382) get inserted into "primary", and the unguarded patch is passed a possibly undefined `calendarId`.
F4: The Office365 and CalDAV `createEvent` read `destinationCalendar[0]` for every credential, so a team member's token posts to the host's calendar, and CalDAV filters down to nothing yet still returns success.
F5: Line 151 now stores `slug` only when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true (the same condition as `requestedSlug`), so organizations created with billing disabled get no slug.
F6: This is about error-message handling and dead code, not wrong functional behavior, and I could not confirm the change added the try/catch.
F7: When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination, `destinationCalendar` is `null`, so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing and team members' calendars are dropped.
F8: Making `destinationCalendar` an array is the change's intended data-model update; an unused `schedulingType` field and inconsistent e2e expectations are not behavior defects.
